questions: Did progress rise above the 0.10 to 0.15 range with wheel_radius 0.035 m? If so, on which track?
Did max_error move from 0.061 to 0.069? If it rose, at what progress does the robot now leave the track?
Did line_loss_events fall to 0 on the s-bend and slalom, or does the drift still start before the first tight bend?
Did steering_oscillation change with the higher ground speed? If it rose sharply, is the controller gain too high for the faster robot?
If the robot now finishes or holds the line, is completion_time limited by speed, or does the ki 0.3 integral change dominate the result?

intent: Test whether drivetrain speed is the limit on progress. Keep the iteration 4 sensor layout and footprint (x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.012 m) and the iteration 2 body, mass and track, and raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m. Expected result: progress rises above 0.15 and max_error stays below 0.06 with line_loss_events at 0 or 1. If max_error rises above 0.069 with more progress, speed is increasing drift and the next change is to reduce mass rather than to change the sensors again.
learning: Sensor span, footprint, lead and body/track changes have all failed to move max_error, so the remaining geometry lever is speed. If wheel_radius 0.035 m does not change the drift, the limit is probably the controller's response to the motor mismatch, not geometry, and the next geometry step should be to test mass 0.5 kg for lower inertia at the higher speed. If speed raises max_error, I will reduce speed (wheel_radius back to 0.03 m) and move to a lower mass instead.
rationale: Iteration 4 (12 mm footprint on the iteration 2 body and track) scored 50.1218, essentially the same as iterations 1 and 2 (50.13 and 50.07). Max_error stayed at 0.0615 to 0.0691 on all three tracks, and each track still had one line-loss event. Across five iterations, sensor span (±0.02 to ±0.03 m), footprint (12 to 16 mm), lead (0.05 to 0.04 m) and turning authority (body and track) each moved max_error by under 0.001 m. Iteration 3 showed that the narrow, short, light body does not help. Steering oscillation stays low (0.07 to 0.15), so the robot is drifting steadily off the tape rather than jittering. Progress is stuck at 0.10 to 0.15 with no completions, so the robot leaves the track early. The Integrator's feedback set a rule for this case: if max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.069 with one line-loss event per track, speed (wheel_radius) is the next untested lever. That condition now holds. I keep the iteration 4 layout, which the Integrator asked for: sensor_size 0.012, sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m and y = 0.04 m, and the iteration 2 body (length 0.18, width 0.12, mass 0.6, track 0.12). I change only wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m. A larger wheel raises ground speed for the same PWM and turn-rate geometry, so it should help the robot cover more of the course before the drift reaches the limit, and it should show whether speed is the binding constraint. There is a risk that higher speed makes the drift at bends worse, which would show as max_error rising above 0.069. The race will also include the Integrator's ki 0.3 change, so the result is a joint effect, and I will attribute the change to speed only if the controller is unchanged from the Integrator's package.
